python3 tools/check_item.py items/ITEMID --report reports/check_item-ITEMID.json
python3 tools/build_package.py verify PACKAGE_FOLDER
Script What it checks Rules
check_all.py runs everything below that applies to the path all
check_ifc.py schema, units, text form, size and triangle limits, levels and containment, rooms (floor, identifiers, occupants, function), doorways, windows, floor slabs, stairs and risers, reservation volumes, zones, optional luminaire and signboard declarations, build volume, finish colours, identifiers B-01 to B-120, D-03 to D-05
check_texture_set.py maps present, 8-bit RGB PNG, same square size, tangent-basis normal, packed occlusion-roughness-metalness, tile size, texel density, luminance, wrap seam, set.json fields D-40 to D-49
check_item.py one item at the origin, class, declared dimensions against geometry, pivot, collision box, triangle budget, item id F-01 to F-51
build_package.py verify manifest against the schema, every hash and size, no unlisted files, one master, package size, provenance and licence, the check report belongs to the master and passed X-10 to X-40

X-40 · REQUIRED - Run check_ifc.py on the exact master file you are sending, with the profile, and include its JSON report in the package. The report records the SHA-256 of the master file it checked and the profile it used; a report for a different file is not accepted. A delivery with any REQUIRED failure in the report is not sent.

Findings have a fixed shape, which a receiving party also uses when it sends work back (section 7):

{ "id": "B-41@1a2b3c4d", "rule": "B-41", "level": "REQUIRED", "status": "fail", "severity": "error",
  "location": { "file": "master.ifc", "element": "3Z2k6lcTnJFPCzw1CFlWEi" },
  "message": "IfcDoor Entrance door is not linked to an opening in a wall",
  "fix_hint": "Add an IfcOpeningElement in the wall with IfcRelVoidsElement ... and
    IfcRelFillsElement ..." }

status is pass, info, warn (a RECOMMENDED rule not met) or fail (a REQUIRED rule not met). element is the GlobalId of the product concerned.

Rules the script can only estimate say "estimate" in their message: the standing-point check (B-33), the sign text fit and legibility (B-101, B-102) and the riser check (B-61). A person confirms those.

5.2 Checks a receiving party typically makes

# Check What it looks at Rule
1 package intake every hash and size, the layout, the manifest X-10 to X-14
2 reading the master opens in an accepted schema edition with a metre length unit and within the limits B-01, B-02, B-05
3 identity GlobalId values and entity numbers are unique across everything held; room and zone identifiers are unique B-22, B-70, B-71, B-81
4 rooms each room has geometry and a floor; rooms can be classified B-20 to B-26
5 doorways each door's opening is found, the rooms either side are listed, the opening is clear B-41, B-42
6 windows window openings cut their walls B-44
7 standing points (walkability extension) every room has a free standing point B-33, B-50
8 stairs and ramps stairs connect levels; risers and slopes within the profile B-60 to B-65
9 reservation volumes provisions are marked, not solid B-80
10 light fixtures (luminaires extension) required properties, positions match B-90 to B-93
11 signs (signboards extension) boards fit their text and are legible B-100 to B-102
12 materials every colour has a finish; every named texture set exists with matching hashes D-03, D-40
13 build volume no vertex outside the volume or inside a keep-out B-110
14 repeatability the same input gives the same result; unchanged identifiers stay B-07, B-75

6. Pre-submission checklist

Tick every line before sending. Lines marked R are REQUIRED rules; the others are RECOMMENDED.

Profile and frame

Structure

Rooms

Fabric

Optional extensions (only when the profile enables them)

Finishes and items

Package

X-41 · RECOMMENDED - Deliver tables/rooms.csv with the columns roomId, name, occupant, kind (room, circulation, observation, open), enclosed (yes or no), level, levelElevationMetres, floorAreaM2, clearHeightM, buildingId and layer, and list every new Occupant string with the room-id prefix that goes with it and its kind, so a receiving party can add its rules before intake. Open areas are listed as rooms too. A starting file is in templates/rooms.template.csv.

7. How a receiving party accepts, returns or refuses

7.1 Outcomes

Outcome When What the sender receives
Accepted every check in section 5 passes and review finds nothing to change a confirmation naming the delivery id, version and the master file's hash
Accepted with notes every REQUIRED rule passes, and the reviewer lists RECOMMENDED rules or defects worth fixing later the same confirmation plus a findings list
Revision needed one or more REQUIRED rules fail, or a defect makes the work unusable, but the delivery is otherwise sound a findings list (section 7.3); the sender sends a new version
Rejected the package cannot be used as it stands: a hash does not match, the file cannot be read, the schema or units are wrong, a hard limit is exceeded, the licence is missing or does not allow use, or the work was built to the wrong profile the reason, and what to do before sending anything again

7.2 Steps

  1. Intake. Package checks (hashes, layout, manifest, provenance, licence). A failure here is a rejection or an immediate return, because nothing else can be trusted.
  2. Reading and identity. The master file is read; units, limits, identifiers.
  3. Rule data. For any new Occupant string or room-id prefix in the room table, the receiving party adds its classification rules, and renames declaration properties to its own names with tools/map_properties.py and a mapping file it keeps itself (a profile's propertyNames and propertyValues are exactly that mapping). The sender's file stays neutral.
  4. Build and check. The receiving party builds from the files and runs the checks of section 5.2.
  5. Review. A person looks at finishes and wrap, signs, lighting, furniture clearances, and anything the scripts only estimate.
  6. Outcome. One of the four outcomes above.

7.3 Findings and revision

The receiving party sends findings in the shape of section 5.1: the rule, its level, the product's GlobalId, and what was measured against what was expected. The sender answers each REQUIRED finding with a fix or a reason.

X-60 · RECOMMENDED - When you send a revision, change only what the findings and your own notes name, bump the version (section 4), list what changed in notes/changes.md, and keep every unchanged identifier. A revision that renames identifiers without being asked is a MAJOR change and is reviewed again from the start.

7.4 After acceptance

An accepted version is held by its hashes. If you later replace a building, deliver a new version of the master file that keeps the identifiers of everything that stays; references the receiving party holds (which room is a start room, which sign belongs to which building) then keep working. Nothing in an accepted version is edited by the receiving party: if it needs a change, it asks for a new version.

Guide 5: Worked example

A complete, minimal delivery: one room with one door, one window, one table, one wall covering and one ceiling light, on one level, with a finish schedule, a texture set, a library item and a package. It is small enough to read in full, and it passes every check in guide 4 under both profiles that come with the set: profiles/default.json and profiles/example-strict.json.

The IFC file is produced by a script, not stored in this set, so that it always matches the script and the version of the IFC library you have installed, and so that every number below can be reproduced. To build and check everything in one go:

pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
python3 tools/run_example.py example-out

This writes example-out/example-room-1.0.0/ (the package), runs every checker on it with the default profile, builds the manifest and ends with build_package.py verify. Run python3 tools/selftest.py to see the checker catch deliberate faults in the same file, and python3 tools/agent_harness.py to see a fresh agent build and pass a delivery from the set alone.

1. The profiles

Item default.json example-strict.json
frame offset 0 12.0 m (declared positions add it)
room identifier up to 64 characters at most 7 characters, required
entity numbers any from #700001
declaration property names as in the guides prefixed Ex_ (the file is renamed by tools/map_properties.py)
extensions all off walkability, luminaires, signboards, furniture collision on
limits 250 MB, 5,000,000 triangles 100 MB, 3,000,000 triangles

To check the example against the strict profile, rename the properties and check with it:

python3 tools/map_properties.py master.ifc master-strict.ifc --mapping profiles/example-strict.json
python3 tools/check_ifc.py master-strict.ifc --profile profiles/example-strict.json

2. What is modelled

  y
  4.2 +--------------[ window 1.5 x 1.2, sill 0.9 ]----------+
      |                                                       |
      |  covering          (table 1.6 x 0.8,                  |
      |  3.0 x 2.4          light above it)                   |
      |                                                       |
  0.0 +---[ door 1.2 x 2.3 ]----------------------------------+
      0.0                                                    5.2  x
Element Class Size and position (file-local metres)
floor slab IfcSlab FLOOR 5.2 by 4.2 by 0.3, top face at z = 0
roof slab IfcSlab ROOF 5.2 by 4.2 by 0.3, underside at z = 3.0 (the ceiling)
south, north, west, east walls IfcWall 0.2 thick, 3.0 high
door opening and door IfcOpeningElement, IfcDoor south wall, x from 0.8 to 2.0, 2.3 high
window opening and window IfcOpeningElement, IfcWindow north wall, x from 2.0 to 3.5, from 0.9 to 2.1 high, opacity 0.45
room IfcSpace inside faces: 4.8 by 3.8 by 3.0, floor at z = 0
table IfcFurnishingElement, mapped item 1.6 by 0.8 by 0.74, pivot at the footprint centre, placed at (2.6, 2.1, 0)
wall covering IfcCovering CLADDING on the west wall's inside face: 10 mm thick, 3.0 m wide, from 0.1 to 2.5 high
luminaire IfcElementAssembly with two IfcLightFixture parts centred over the table, emissive part centre at (2.6, 2.1, 2.89)

3. Step by step

3.1 Frame, level and identity (B-10 to B-14, B-70, B-71)

The file is IFC4 in metres. The project carries a property set with FrameNote and LevelOffsetMetres = 12.0. One building and one level named Example building - ground / +0 m with elevation 0. Entity numbers start at #700001 (the strict profile's range); every GlobalId is derived from a stable key, so the file is identical on every run.

3.2 Walls, openings, door and window (B-40 to B-44)

Each wall is an extruded rectangle. The door and the window each have an IfcOpeningElement that voids a wall (IfcRelVoidsElement) and is filled by the door or window (IfcRelFillsElement). The doorway is 2.3 m high and nothing crosses it. In the file:

#700198=IFCRELVOIDSELEMENT('1C_9SKyzTHcQf6qIs0XZ4T',$,$,$,#700125,#700197);
#700216=IFCDOOR('3Z2k6lcTnJFPCzw1CFlWEi',$,'Entrance
    door',$,$,#700213,#700215,$,2.3,1.2,.DOOR.,.SINGLE_SWING_LEFT.,$);
#700217=IFCRELFILLSELEMENT('29lMJRl7DVmRJwjxlT70xI',$,$,$,#700197,#700216);

3.3 Floor, roof and ceiling (B-50, B-53, B-54)

The floor is a slab whose top is the finished floor at z = 0, and the roof slab's underside is the ceiling. Many consumers draw no ceiling mesh, so that underside is what a person looks up at; guide 2 says how to give it a finish through the slab's bottom slot.

3.4 The room (B-20 to B-27)

#700273=IFCSPACE('1C1BaaS91KOgLuDEt1VXqX',$,'Example work room',$,$,#700270,#700272,'Example work
    room',.ELEMENT.,.INTERNAL.,0.);
#700274=IFCRELAGGREGATES('3jyuNv4XzQSRLalH7sDq_3',$,$,$,#700034,(#700273));
#700275=IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE('RoomId',$,IFCTEXT('EX-001'),$);
#700276=IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE('Occupant',$,IFCTEXT('Example Occupant'),$);
#700277=IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE('Function',$,IFCTEXT('Work room'),$);

The room is an IfcSpace (the IFC name for a room or zone) aggregated under the level. Its geometry is an extrusion of the 4.8 by 3.8 floor outline up to 3.0 m. The properties are single values in a property set linked by IfcRelDefinesByProperties. RoomId is EX-001, six characters. The room table row repeats them, and the net area 18.24 m2 equals 4.8 times 3.8.

3.5 The table (guide 3)

The table's geometry is defined once, as a representation map with its origin at the footprint centre and its lowest point at z = 0, and the element is an instance of it (IfcMappedItem), placed at (2.6, 2.1, 0). In the item library the same table is a separate file, items/table.work.1600/table.work.1600.ifc, with a description file declaring its pivot, dimensions, collision box, side clearances, a seat anchor and placement rules.

3.6 The wall covering (D-30 to D-32)

The covering is a thin IfcCovering shell, 10 mm thick, whose back face sits exactly on the west wall's inside face (x = 0.2, the shell runs from x = 0.2 to 0.21). It has its own colour, #8c6f4e, so it becomes its own entry in the finish schedule. The simpler alternative for a whole wall is to give the wall element itself the finish colour. Support for IfcCovering varies, so confirm it with the consumer before relying on it.

3.7 The luminaire (optional extension; B-90 to B-93)

One assembly with a housing part and an emissive part whose name ends in lens. The assembly carries the declaration properties. The emissive part's centre is at local (2.6, 2.1, 2.89). Under a profile with a frame offset, the declared position is in the consumer's global frame, so the height gets the offset added once:

Property Value
LightPositionLocal 2.6,2.1,2.89 (optional, for checking)
LightPosition 2.6,2.1,14.89 (2.89 + 12.0)
LightAim 0,0,-1 (unit length)
LightType, LightEnergy, LightRangeM, LightSpotDeg spot, 6, 8, 78
LightColor 1,0.87,0.7 (warm)
LightFadeBeginM, LightFadeLengthM 40, 20
LuminaireTarget EX-001

With the luminaires extension enabled, the checker confirms that the emissive part's centre plus the offset is within the profile's tolerance of LightPosition. Under the default profile (extension off) the fixture is simply a light fixture.

3.8 Colours and the finish schedule (guide 2)

Each (class, colour, opacity) combination needs a finish. The checker finds nine:

Class Colour Opacity Used for
IfcWall #d9d2c3 1.0 all four walls (one finish)
IfcSlab #c9c4b8 1.0 floor slab
IfcSlab #e8e4da 1.0 roof slab, whose underside is the ceiling
IfcDoor #977353 1.0 door leaf
IfcWindow #91c8d0 0.45 glass
IfcFurnishingElement #ccbba0 1.0 the table
IfcCovering #8c6f4e 1.0 the wall covering
IfcLightFixture #3d4348 1.0 luminaire housing
IfcLightFixture #fff0cf 1.0 luminaire emissive part

finishes/finish-schedule.json has one entry for each, and a floor rule for Example Occupant. The slab entries use all three face slots: top for the floor, bottom for the ceiling, side for the edge.

3.9 The texture set (D-40 to D-50)

finishes/textures/plaster_example/ has albedo.png, normal.png, orm.png and set.json (1024 by 1024 pixels, 2 m per tile, so 512 pixels per metre; tintMode multiply). It is made by tools/make_sample_texture_set.py from seamless noise with a fixed seed. check_texture_set.py --preview wrap.png writes the three-by-three arrangement so you can see that the edges do not show.

3.10 Package, manifest and checks (guide 4)

run_example.py writes the check reports into reports/, writes package-meta.json, and runs build_package.py init then verify. The final package listing:

example-room-1.0.0/
  manifest.json   SHA256SUMS.txt
  ifc/example-room-master.ifc
  tables/{rooms.csv,building.json}
  finishes/{finish-schedule.json,library.json,SOURCES.csv}
  finishes/textures/plaster_example/{albedo.png,normal.png,orm.png,set.json}
  items/table.work.1600/{table.work.1600.ifc,table.work.1600.item.json}
  reports/{check_ifc.json,check_texture_set.json,check_item-table.work.1600.json}
  notes/changes.md

Expected output of the IFC check:

result: PASS (0 REQUIRED failure(s), 0 RECOMMENDED warning(s)); 1 levels, 1 rooms, 1 doors,
1 windows, 1 luminaires, 216 triangles, 136 vertices, 1 furniture, 9 finishKeys

4. Things to try

  • Open example-room-master.ifc in any IFC viewer; it is also plain text.
  • Edit tools/make_sample.py: rename RoomId to EX-0001 and check with the strict profile (too long for 7 characters, B-23).
  • Move the table to (1.4, 0.3) so that it stands in the doorway (B-42). The same fault is a case in tools/selftest.py.
  • Remove the IfcRelFillsElement of the door (B-41), or change the emissive part's name to end in glow (B-90, strict profile).
  • Change LightPosition height to 20 and see the mismatch (B-92, strict profile).

5. What the example leaves out

A free-standing sign (B-100), reservation volumes (B-80) and a library with several items. Each is a small extension of what is here; the rule text in guides 1 to 3 says how. Stairs, several levels, several rooms, open-air rooms, sloped sites and non-rectangular forms are in the larger examples below.

6. Larger examples

python3 tools/make_fixtures.py out/ builds three more buildings with the authoring kit tools/ifc_author.py. Each passes check_ifc.py without warnings; tools/test_fixtures.py also runs them through the terrain tools and breaks each of the rules they exercise.

Fixture What it shows
tray-house two levels of cantilevered trays over a watercourse: stacked slabs, open-air terraces (B-143), a stair through a slab well sized for head-room (B-61, B-53), a stone core, parapets
hillside-block a block stepped up a steep slope and turned 30 degrees from east: two ground-contact levels (B-141), footings and a retaining wall (B-142), a gable roof of sloped slabs (B-144), a stair that arrives on a roof terrace
courtyard four wings round an open courtyard on one level: battered outer walls (B-144), flat roofs with a courtyard opening, parapets, open-air circulation reached by doors (B-47)

To see a building, run python3 tools/preview.py MASTER.ifc OUT_DIR: one plan per level and an isometric view.

Repair loop

How to get a deliverable to zero REQUIRED findings. The same loop works for a building, a material library, a furniture library and a package. It needs only the tools in tools/; no network and no service.

The loop

  1. Run one command for the deliverable, printing JSON:

    python3 tools/check_all.py PATH --json --out report.json

    (PATH is a master .ifc file, a folder with finishes/, a folder with items/, or a package folder with manifest.json. Add --profile PROFILE.json for a building so the frame, identifiers and volumes are checked.)

  2. Read the report. Look at result, exitCode and summary.requiredFailures first. Then list the findings whose status is fail: each has rule, message, location.element (a GlobalId, when one product is concerned), location.file and fix_hint. For more on a rule, open its entry in rules.json (statement, rationale, examples, related).

  3. Fix the source of the deliverable (the model, the schedule, the item, the package inputs), not the report. Fix the lowest-numbered structural findings first (B-01 to B-06, B-13, B-20 to B-26): later findings often disappear with them. Make one kind of change at a time.

  4. Rebuild whatever the fix touched (re-export the IFC, rebuild the manifest with build_package.py init).

  5. Rerun step 1 and compare. Repeat until summary.requiredFailures is 0 and the exit code is 0.

Then look at warn findings (RECOMMENDED rules). Fix the ones whose fix_hint is cheap; list the rest in notes/open-points.md.

Report fields

Field Meaning
result pass, fail or error
exitCode 0 no REQUIRED rule failed; 1 at least one did; 2 wrong command line; 3 an input could not be read
summary counts: requiredFailures, recommendedWarnings, passes, info
findings[].id stable: the rule id, then a short hash of rule, file, element and message; the same problem keeps the same id between runs
findings[].status pass, info, warn (RECOMMENDED not met) or fail (REQUIRED not met)
findings[].fix_hint what to change, present on warn and fail
reports[] the full report of each tool that check_all.py ran

To list only what must be fixed, read the file with any JSON tool, for example:

python3 -c "import json;r=json.load(open('report.json'));[print(f['rule'],f['location'],f['message']
    ,'->',f['fix_hint']) for f in r['findings'] if f['status']=='fail']"

Stop conditions

Stop and report instead of looping when any of these holds:

  • The same finding id is still present after three runs in a row. Report the finding, what you changed, and why you think it did not help.
  • The exit code is 3, or result is error. Fix the path or the missing input; this is not a rule failure.
  • A fix needs information that is not in the profile or the files (an Occupant string, a level offset, a licence statement, the assigned entity-number start). Ask the person who gave you the profile; do not invent it.
  • More than ten runs without the number of REQUIRED failures going down.
  • A finding seems wrong. Say which rule and element, and what you measured. Do not work around it.

Never do these to get a pass

  • Edit a report, change a rule level, delete a check, or edit a tool to hide a finding.
  • Change a value only to satisfy the checker when it makes the model less true (for example, widening a door in the file while the drawing says otherwise).
  • Delete the element that is flagged without saying so in notes/changes.md.
  • Run the checker on a different file than the one you deliver (rule X-40 ties the report to the file by hash).

Worked mini-loop

Run 1 prints a failure:

{ "rule": "B-42", "status": "fail", "location": {"element": "3Z2k6lcTnJFPCzw1CFlWEi"},
  "message": "doorway Entrance door is blocked at 0.6 m by Work table, 1.6 m",
  "fix_hint": "Make the opening at least 1.9 m high and remove anything (sill, bar, furniture) that
    crosses the doorway centre line." }

Fix: move the table out of the doorway and re-export. Run 2 shows summary.requiredFailures 0 and exit code 0. Then rebuild the manifest (python3 tools/build_package.py init PACKAGE_DIR package-meta.json), run python3 tools/check_all.py PACKAGE_DIR --json, and deliver.

Rules index

Every rule of the four guides in one table. Generated by tools/rules_index.py; do not edit by hand.

The same rules, with machine fields, are in rules.json.

197 rules: 59 REQUIRED and 138 RECOMMENDED.

Guide REQUIRED RECOMMENDED Total
1 Builder's and Architect's 33 69 102
2 Interior Decorator's 10 34 44
3 Furniture and Fixtures 6 27 33
4 Delivery and Acceptance 10 8 18
All 59 138 197
Rule Level Guide Statement
B-01 REQUIRED 1 Deliver an IFC schema edition the profile accepts (schema.allowed, default IFC4).
B-02 REQUIRED 1 Declare the length unit as metres (an IfcSIUnit LENGTHUNIT METRE, or a prefixed or conversion-based unit that resolves to metres) and model in it.
B-02a RECOMMENDED 1 Prefer plain metres (a METRE unit with no prefix) over a prefixed or conversion-based unit, which some tools mishandle.
B-03 RECOMMENDED 1 Deliver one coordinated master file per placement area, and send per-building files only as alternates.
B-04 REQUIRED 1 Keep the file plain ASCII: write every non-ASCII character with the format's escape (\X2\00B7\X0\ for a middle dot, \X2\2014\X0\ for a long dash).
B-05 REQUIRED 1 Stay within the profile's hard limits: limits.maxFileMegabytes, limits.maxVertices and limits.maxTriangles.
B-06 REQUIRED 1 Use geometry that every common reader can display: swept solids (IfcExtrudedAreaSolid with rectangle, circle, arbitrary closed or arbitrary-with-voids profiles), faceted breps or polygonal face sets, and mapped items.
B-07 RECOMMENDED 1 Make the export deterministic: the same inputs give a byte-identical file (fixed timestamps, stable ordering, GlobalId values derived from stable keys).
B-08 RECOMMENDED 1 Write each STEP entity on a single line when the profile asks (file.singleLineEntities).
B-09 RECOMMENDED 1 Keep the file below the profile's recommended size, budgets.recommendedFileMegabytes.
B-10 REQUIRED 1 Use a right-handed frame with Z up and the horizontal axes the profile states (frame.horizontalAxes), in metres.
B-11 RECOMMENDED 1 Author in the placement the profile expects (frame.placement): with final, local z = 0 is the finished floor of the lowest level and the consumer applies no offset or rotation, so author in the final placement frame.
B-12 RECOMMENDED 1 State your frame in the file: a property set on the IfcProject with a text property FrameNote ("metres; +X forward; +Y left; +Z up; local z = 0 at the finished floor of the lowest level") and a number LevelOffsetMetres.
B-13 REQUIRED 1 Create one IfcBuildingStorey for every level of every building, with a Name and a numeric Elevation equal to the level's finished-floor height in your file's frame, and make every element belong to one: contained (IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure), aggregated (IfcRelAggregates) or, for zones, referenced (IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure).
B-14 RECOMMENDED 1 Use the full hierarchy IfcProject > IfcSite > IfcBuilding > IfcBuildingStorey, one IfcBuilding per building, and level names that start with the building name (Clinic - ground / +0 m).
B-15 RECOMMENDED 1 Keep floor-to-floor heights regular so that stairs, lifts and openings line up between levels; make tall halls an exception you can name.
B-142 RECOMMENDED 1 Put nothing below the lowest finished floor except slabs, footings, piles, walls, stairs, ramps, openings, the terrain element and reservation volumes.
B-20 REQUIRED 1 Model every room as an IfcSpace (internal, ELEMENT) whose geometry is an upward extrusion of the room's floor outline: the lowest plane of the solid is the floor and the top is the underside of the ceiling or slab above.
B-21 REQUIRED 1 Give every IfcSpace geometry.
B-22 REQUIRED 1 Give every room that has a RoomId a value that is unique, and write it as an IfcPropertySingleValue inside an IfcPropertySet linked by IfcRelDefinesByProperties.
B-23 REQUIRED 1 Make room identifiers meet the profile: at most identifiers.roomIdMaxLength characters and matching identifiers.roomIdPattern.
B-24 RECOMMENDED 1 Give every room an Occupant (text): the organisation or use it belongs to.
B-25 RECOMMENDED 1 Give every room a Function (text) describing its use.
B-26 RECOMMENDED 1 Give every room a RoomId.
B-27 RECOMMENDED 1 Also supply, when known: NetAreaSquareMetres (number), BaseLevelMetres (number), ClearHeightMetres (number) and Notes (text).
B-28 RECOMMENDED 1 Give each room a complete, human-readable Name; names appear in lists and on labels.
B-29 RECOMMENDED 1 Declare streets, paths, plazas and park areas as rooms too, with an identifier and a Function, so that they can be referred to, lit and signed.
B-143 RECOMMENDED 1 Model an open-air room (terrace, courtyard, deck, path, plaza) as an IfcSpace with PredefinedType EXTERNAL and the boolean property Enclosed set to false, and an internal room with Enclosed true or absent.
B-30 RECOMMENDED 1 Let rooms on one level touch along wall centre lines but not overlap by more than the wall thickness; overlapping floors make "which room is this point in" ambiguous.
B-31 RECOMMENDED 1 Draw the room outline at the inside wall faces so the floor area is the usable area.
B-32 RECOMMENDED 1 Group rooms into buildings with a BuildingId property, and mark long-lived content separately from replaceable content with a Layer property (permanent or interim), so that a building can be swapped without touching its surroundings.
B-33 REQUIRED 1 Leave every enclosed room a floor area where a person can stand: at least extensions.walkability.standingClearanceMetres clear of furniture, equipment, rails and transport elements.
B-34 RECOMMENDED 1 Keep a free floor circle of extensions.walkability.freeCircleMetres in every room, and leave clear aisles from seating to doors.
B-40 REQUIRED 1 Model walls as IfcWall (IfcWallStandardCase is also read), not as generic proxies; consumers select, colour and count by class.
B-40a RECOMMENDED 1 Use one element per maximal straight run rather than one per room edge.
B-41 REQUIRED 1 Model every door as an IfcDoor that fills an IfcOpeningElement in the wall, linked with IfcRelVoidsElement (wall to opening) and IfcRelFillsElement (opening to door).
B-42 REQUIRED 1 Keep every doorway passable: its clear height is at least geometry.doorMinClearHeightMetres, and nothing solid (a sill, a bar, a glazed panel, furniture) crosses the opening centre line at the heights in geometry.doorwayProbeHeightsMetres.
B-43 RECOMMENDED 1 Make doorways at least geometry.doorMinClearWidthMetres wide.
B-44 REQUIRED 1 Model every window as an IfcWindow in an IfcOpeningElement linked with the voids and fills relations, so the wall is cut where the window is.
B-45 RECOMMENDED 1 Give glass a surface style with opacity below 1 (about 0.4 to 0.6), so that every consumer shows it as see-through.
B-46 RECOMMENDED 1 Give walls their real thickness; zero-thickness walls and double walls confuse area, collision and rendering.
B-47 RECOMMENDED 1 Make every room reachable through a doorway, an open edge or a stair from a circulation room.
B-48 RECOMMENDED 1 Do not put a door in a floor or roof; floor apertures are slab openings (B-53).
B-50 RECOMMENDED 1 Model every walkable floor, including walkable roofs, as an IfcSlab (FLOOR or ROOF) whose top face is the finished floor.
B-51 RECOMMENDED 1 Do not duplicate a floor the consumer already provides (baseSurfaces); two coplanar surfaces flicker.
B-51a RECOMMENDED 1 Omit slabs that rest directly on a consumer-supplied floor, or make them very thin.
B-52 RECOMMENDED 1 Give slabs a realistic thickness; very thin slabs are fine only for surface layers such as paving.
B-53 REQUIRED 1 Cut every hole in a slab (stair wells, shafts, service drops) as an IfcOpeningElement linked by IfcRelVoidsElement, not as separate floor pieces that merely leave a gap.
B-54 RECOMMENDED 1 Model ceilings or roofs.
B-144 RECOMMENDED 1 Model a pitched or sloped roof with sloped IfcSlab ROOF pieces that follow the real pitch, and a wall whose faces lean (a battered wall) as one IfcWall with an inclined section, not as flat boxes or steps.
B-55 RECOMMENDED 1 Keep your own structure clear of openings in surfaces the consumer supplies (baseSurfaces), with the margin the profile states.
B-60 REQUIRED 1 Model each stair flight as an IfcStairFlight (a parent IfcStair without geometry is fine).
B-61 RECOMMENDED 1 Keep risers at or below geometry.stairRiserLimitMetres, with a landing and head-room; avoid winding and spiral stairs unless you have checked the consumer reads them.
B-62 RECOMMENDED 1 Give every multi-level building at least one real stair.
B-63 RECOMMENDED 1 Draw lifts as IfcTransportElement with PredefinedType ELEVATOR, with properties such as Service, StopsMetres and ShaftWidthMetres.
B-64 RECOMMENDED 1 Keep every walked slope at or below geometry.rampMaxSlope (rise over run) except stairs, and give ramps a clear width at least as wide as a doorway.
B-65 RECOMMENDED 1 Do not leave low obstacles up to extensions.walkability.stepHeightMetres high (floor boxes, square-edged wedges) that a walker steps over unseen; ramp them or make them visible steps.
B-66 RECOMMENDED 1 Model rails (IfcRailing) with cheap geometry: simple posts and one rail section.
B-67 RECOMMENDED 1 Know which classes the consumer treats as not solid (extensions.walkability.nonSolidClasses) and model walk-through areas with those classes or with reservation volumes (B-80); everything else may block movement.
B-70 REQUIRED 1 Give every product a unique 22-character IFC GlobalId that does not change between exports.
B-71 RECOMMENDED 1 Number your IFC entities from the start the profile assigns (identifiers.entityNumberStart, when set) so that files from several authors can be merged without clashes.
B-72 RECOMMENDED 1 Write declaration properties as text, number or boolean values in IfcPropertySingleValue entries of an IfcPropertySet linked by IfcRelDefinesByProperties on the product itself.
B-73 RECOMMENDED 1 Use one descriptive property set per topic (Pset_Declaration_Room, ...) and put only declaration properties in it.
B-74 RECOMMENDED 1 If your organisation uses a classification scheme, attach it with IfcRelAssociatesClassification.
B-75 RECOMMENDED 1 Keep identifiers stable across revisions: an unchanged room, door or fixture keeps its RoomId, GlobalId and declaration ids.
B-76 RECOMMENDED 1 Give your own identifiers dotted prefixes (arch.entrance, clinic.lobby), at most 160 characters, no control characters.
B-80 RECOMMENDED 1 Declare a volume that must stay empty or must not be solid (a sight line, a clearance, a service corridor) twice: as an IfcSpatialZone, and (so it can be seen) as an IfcBuildingElementProxy with PredefinedType PROVISIONFORSPACE.
B-81 RECOMMENDED 1 Give every zone a unique identifier (ZoneId or, if missing, its Name) and its own geometry; a zone without geometry cannot be shown or selected.
B-81a RECOMMENDED 1 Always supply ZoneId, plus ZoneClass (for example observation-sightline) and Requirement (a sentence saying what must stay clear).
B-82 RECOMMENDED 1 Use zones to record viewing intent (a downward sight line from a mezzanine); ordinary glass cannot be one-way, and who may look is a consumer decision, not a file property.
B-90 REQUIRED 1 Model each fixture as an IfcElementAssembly that aggregates two IfcLightFixture parts: a housing, and an emissive part whose Name ends in the profile's suffix (extensions.luminaires.lensNameSuffix).
B-91 REQUIRED 1 Put every property in extensions.luminaires.requiredProperties on the assembly, make LuminaireId unique, and use a LightType from extensions.luminaires.lightTypes.
B-92 REQUIRED 1 Write LightPosition in the consumer's global frame: the file-local point plus frame.levelOffsetMetres (same x and y, z plus the offset); the geometry stays file-local.
B-92a RECOMMENDED 1 Give the file-local position as well (LightPositionLocal) so a reviewer can check the offset was applied once.
B-93 REQUIRED 1 Make LightAim a unit vector (length 1 within 1e-6) in the consumer's frame.
B-94 RECOMMENDED 1 Give every enclosed room at least one fixture (set LuminaireTarget), between the floor and the ceiling, in warm colours, not pointed at glazing.
B-95 RECOMMENDED 1 Count the lights: every declared fixture may become a real light, and the consumer may cap them per room (extensions.luminaires.maxPerRoom).
B-100 REQUIRED 1 Model a board as an IfcElementAssembly carrying every property in extensions.signboards.requiredProperties, with a SignboardKind from extensions.signboards.kinds.
B-101 REQUIRED 1 Make the main text fit the board: allow about 0.55 times the capital height of width per character plus a margin of 12 % of the board height on each side; text that cannot be fitted at a capital height of 0.05 m is an error.
B-102 RECOMMENDED 1 Declare a reading distance your letters support: capital height in metres must be at least pixels * readM / extensions.signboards.displayPixelsPerRadian, with pixels from extensions.signboards.minCapitalPixels (primary text), and the distance within extensions.signboards.readingDistanceMetres.
B-103 RECOMMENDED 1 Declare an entrance board on the wall's outer face, not the wall centre plane, and keep lamps and trees away from its face.
B-110 REQUIRED 1 Keep all geometry inside the profile's build volume (buildVolume) and outside its keep-out regions (keepOut), when it gives them; check every vertex, not only footprints.
B-111 RECOMMENDED 1 Make solids closed and consistently oriented: no missing faces, no inside-out solids, no zero-area or duplicate faces.
B-112 RECOMMENDED 1 Avoid coplanar overlapping faces (two walls sharing a face, a covering lying exactly on a wall, a slab exactly on a floor).
B-113 RECOMMENDED 1 Use mapped items (IfcMappedItem with IfcRepresentationMap) for repeated parts.
B-114 RECOMMENDED 1 Do not model what cannot be seen or used: hidden interiors, bolts, hinge detail, text as geometry, curves with more than geometry.maxCurveSegmentsPerCircle segments per full circle.
B-115 RECOMMENDED 1 Do not model terrain, soil or relief in IFC unless the profile says how.
B-116 RECOMMENDED 1 Do not model a thin layer at a height where the consumer adds its own surface layer (floor finishes laid on the room floor); two layers at one height flicker.
B-120 RECOMMENDED 1 Stay under the profile's recommended triangle count, budgets.recommendedTriangles.
B-121 RECOMMENDED 1 Spend triangles where the viewer looks: entrances, interiors a person stands in, anything within arm's reach.
B-130 REQUIRED 1 Deliver the terrain as exactly one IfcGeographicElement with PredefinedType TERRAIN, contained in the IfcSite, whose body is one IfcTriangulatedFaceSet.
B-131 REQUIRED 1 Make the terrain a valid heightfield over a rectangular patch: every triangle faces up and has area, no edge belongs to more than two triangles, and the triangles cover the patch rectangle exactly once.
B-132 REQUIRED 1 Make the terrain cover the building: the plan points of the slabs and walls of every ground-contact level, grown by extensions.terrain.footprintMarginMetres, lie inside the patch.
B-133 REQUIRED 1 Georeference the file with an IfcMapConversion from the model context to an IfcProjectedCRS named extensions.terrain.crsName, in metres, with the local X axis set to the building azimuth (a unit vector, east when the building is not turned), scale 1 and OrthogonalHeight equal to the height above sea level of the lowest finished floor (local z = 0).
B-134 REQUIRED 1 Set IfcSite.RefElevation to the terrain height at the building origin above sea level, within extensions.terrain.siteElevationToleranceMetres of the terrain element at that point.
B-135 REQUIRED 1 Do not put a building in water: the terrain at every footprint point of every ground-contact level is at or above extensions.terrain.seaLevelMetres, and FootprintInWater is not true.
B-136 RECOMMENDED 1 Do not let the building float or sink: no ground-contact level's floor is above the terrain by more than extensions.terrain.floatToleranceMetres at every footprint point of that level, or below it by more than extensions.terrain.buryToleranceMetres at every one.
B-137 REQUIRED 1 Pin the terrain source in a property set Pset_Declaration_Terrain on the terrain element: Role (derived-context), PackageName, PackageVersion, PackageSha256, PatchSha256, PatchLevel, PixelSizeMetres, ErrorBoundMetres (at most extensions.terrain.maxErrorBoundMetres), Frame and VerticalDatum.
B-138 RECOMMENDED 1 Keep the terrain within extensions.terrain.maxTriangles.
B-139 RECOMMENDED 1 Keep water out of the file and declare it as metadata in Pset_Declaration_Site on the IfcSite: SeaLevelMetres, FootprintInWater and, when known, DistanceToShoreMetres.
B-140 RECOMMENDED 1 State the frame of the terrain numbers: Pset_Declaration_Terrain.Frame says that the file frame is x east, y north, z up and relative to the lowest finished floor.
B-141 RECOMMENDED 1 Declare every level that touches the ground with GroundContact true in Pset_Declaration_Level; without a declaration the lowest level is the only ground-contact level.
D-01 REQUIRED 2 Give each distinct finish its own colour within an element class.
D-02 REQUIRED 2 Give the same finish the same colour and opacity on every element that uses it.
D-03 REQUIRED 2 When you deliver a finish schedule, include an entry for every (class, colour, opacity) combination that appears in your IFC files.
D-04 RECOMMENDED 2 Use opacity below 1 only for glass and other see-through things (about 0.4 to 0.6 for glazing).
D-05 RECOMMENDED 2 Keep the palette small: at most budgets.maxDistinctColours combinations (default 50).
D-06 RECOMMENDED 2 Treat the IFC colour as a design tint: the schedule says how strongly it is blended into the texture (0 means the texture alone, 1 the colour fully).
D-07 RECOMMENDED 2 Avoid pure black, pure white and very dark large surfaces: they clip or disappear under typical lighting.
D-08 RECOMMENDED 2 Choose neutral tints for fabrics; strongly coloured tints shift under lighting.
D-10 RECOMMENDED 2 When you deliver a finish schedule, give every room that has a floor a floor finish: list them in the floors section by Occupant, by RoomId list or by pattern, plus a default.
D-11 RECOMMENDED 2 Also write a text property Finish on each room (for example light warm-grey resilient floor; pale ivory walls), so that the intent stays with the room.
D-12 RECOMMENDED 2 Change floor finishes at door lines, not mid-room, and keep a visible threshold between unlike finishes.
D-13 RECOMMENDED 2 Choose low-gloss, light floors for rooms people work in: dark glossy floors read as black under many lighting set-ups.
D-20 RECOMMENDED 2 Decide ceilings through the slab or roof above: the bottom face of the slab above is the ceiling of the room below.
D-21 RECOMMENDED 2 Keep ceiling finishes matte and light; glossy ceilings amplify lamp hot spots.
D-30 RECOMMENDED 2 Express a wall finish through the wall element's own colour (one colour per finish and per class).
D-31 RECOMMENDED 2 Use an IfcCovering (PredefinedType CLADDING, FLOORING, CEILING or WRAPPING) only when a finish covers part of a wall, or a surface that has no element of its own.
D-32 RECOMMENDED 2 Do not rely on a texture pattern starting at an edge: consumers project textures differently.
D-33 RECOMMENDED 2 Make skirtings, cornices, door frames, handrails and accent bands separate elements with their own colour, at least 1 cm thick.
D-34 RECOMMENDED 2 Accent features (a feature wall, a coloured door, a timber panel) are a colour on the element in the same class as its neighbours, not an image inside the IFC.
D-35 RECOMMENDED 2 Describe glass by colour, opacity and three optional settings: base opacity, edge reflection (fresnelAlpha) and smudge roughness (smudgeRough).
D-40 REQUIRED 2 Deliver every texture set as a folder <setName>/ containing the maps the profile lists (textures.maps, default albedo.png, normal.png, orm.png) and set.json.
D-41 REQUIRED 2 Use these encodings, so that every consumer reads the maps the same way:
D-42 RECOMMENDED 2 Make the texture tile seamlessly in both directions; consumers repeat it across large surfaces, and a seam repeats with it.
D-43 REQUIRED 2 Declare the physical size of one tile in set.json as tileMetres, so that a consumer can scale it correctly.
D-44 RECOMMENDED 2 Use square, power-of-two images, all maps the same size, one of textures.sizesPixels (default 512, 1024, 2048).
D-45 RECOMMENDED 2 Choose the tile size so the texel density is inside textures.densityPixelsPerMetre (default 250 to 2500 pixels per metre): for 1024 pixels that is a tile of about 0.4 m to 4 m.
D-46 RECOMMENDED 2 Avoid fine, regular weaves and stripes with a tile under 0.5 m: they produce moire at grazing angles.
D-47 RECOMMENDED 2 Declare tintMode in set.json (one of textures.tintModes): multiply when the albedo is a near-neutral light map meant to be tinted by the IFC colour, or authored when the colour in the map is final.
D-48 RECOMMENDED 2 Keep the pattern free of one-off features (a single stain, one knot) that would repeat visibly, and do not bake low-frequency variation in; consumers can add it.
D-49 RECOMMENDED 2 If a pattern has a direction (planks, brushed metal, grain), say which image axis it follows in set.json (direction: u, v or none); consumers decide how directional patterns are oriented on floors and walls.
D-50 RECOMMENDED 2 Check your tiles in a three-by-three arrangement and at a long viewing distance: fine relief that reads as speckle should be softened.
D-60 REQUIRED 2 Deliver finish-schedule.json with these sections: format (finish-schedule/1), delivery, version (SemVer), materials[] (one entry per (class, colour, opacity) key: key, role, usedBy, faces), floors[] (ordered floor rules: where and finish), and libraries[] (the texture-set folders it names, with versions).
D-61 REQUIRED 2 Name only texture sets that exist: each face entry names a set from your delivery or from a library the profile or consumer publishes.
D-62 RECOMMENDED 2 Mark materials that must stay as they are (emissive strips, planning markers) with "keep": true and a reason instead of giving them a texture.
D-63 RECOMMENDED 2 Treat the schedule as a proposal: a consumer applies what it can.
D-70 RECOMMENDED 2 Build the palette from a few families and give each organisation or zone a distinct tint rather than a distinct pattern.
D-71 RECOMMENDED 2 Describe the intent in words as well as colours ("light warm-grey resilient floor; pale ivory washable walls; low gloss"), so that a consumer with its own material library can choose.
D-72 RECOMMENDED 2 Do not use texture or colour to carry meaning that labels already carry (room names, identifiers, directions).
D-80 REQUIRED 2 Record the source and licence of every texture set and every image in it in a SOURCES.csv next to the library with the columns asset,type,source,licence,notes.
D-81 REQUIRED 2 Include the SHA-256 hash of every file in the manifest (guide 4).
D-82 RECOMMENDED 2 Prefer procedural sets with the generator and its seeds included; byte-identical output lets a consumer verify and regenerate the library and keeps the delivery small.
D-83 RECOMMENDED 2 Name sets in lower case with underscores (limewash_mottled) and finishes with dotted names (wall.limewash.warm).
D-84 RECOMMENDED 2 Include a contact sheet (a PNG with each set's albedo, normal and roughness side by side, plus the tile size) so a reviewer sees the library at a glance.
D-85 RECOMMENDED 2 Keep the library independent of any one building: no file name, label or set name should refer to a particular project.
F-01 REQUIRED 3 Use these classes for items, because consumers and tools are written for them, and make the description's class agree with the model.
F-02 RECOMMENDED 3 Set ObjectType to a category word from this list so that reports and schedules can group items: table, desk, seat, bench, sofa, bed, shelf, cabinet, counter, partition, planter, equipment, appliance, lamp, sign, accent, other.
F-03 RECOMMENDED 3 Add a property set Pset_Declaration_Item with text properties ItemId (the library id, section 3), ItemVersion (SemVer), Role (what the item is for, for example work table), and optionally Occupant and PlanningStatus.
F-10 RECOMMENDED 3 Make each item file IFC4 (guide 1, B-01 to B-06) containing exactly one furniture or equipment element, placed at the origin with no rotation, in metres, with a stable GlobalId.
F-11 RECOMMENDED 3 Give every item a library id of the form category.name.size in lower case (for example seat.stool.450), unique within the library and never reused for a different design.
F-12 RECOMMENDED 3 Provide a description file <ItemId>.item.json for every item (section 3.1).
F-20 REQUIRED 3 Model in metres in the right-handed frame of guide 1 (B-02, B-10), with the item's own origin at its pivot (F-21).
F-20a RECOMMENDED 3 Do not scale an item with an IfcCartesianTransformationOperator or any non-unit transform.
F-21 RECOMMENDED 3 Put the pivot where the item meets the building, so placing it needs one point and one turn.
F-22 RECOMMENDED 3 Declare the bounding dimensions in the description and keep them equal (within 1 cm) to the measured size of the geometry.
F-23 RECOMMENDED 3 Use true-to-life sizes: a work table is about 1.6 by 0.8 by 0.74 m, a chair about 0.5 by 0.55 by 0.85 m.
F-30 RECOMMENDED 3 Declare anchors in item coordinates (metres, relative to the pivot).
F-31 RECOMMENDED 3 Declare placement rules under placement: mounting (floor, wall, ceiling, surface), againstWall, minWallDistance (metres), rotations (allowed turns about the vertical axis, in degrees), roomUses (kinds of use it suits, free words matching the Function text of rooms), avoid (kinds of room it must not go in), and mountHeight for wall items.
F-32 RECOMMENDED 3 Declare clearance minimums around the item: front, back, left, right, top (metres of free volume needed).
F-33 RECOMMENDED 3 Keep items off door openings and off the floor directly in front of a door; a table in the doorway fails the doorway check (guide 1, B-42).
F-34 RECOMMENDED 3 Do not place items so that they cover a room's whole free floor (guide 1, B-33).
F-40 REQUIRED 3 Assume the profile's collision mode (extensions.furnitureCollision.mode).
F-41 RECOMMENDED 3 Place furniture with rotations in multiples of 90 degrees where you can; a box around a 45-degree table is larger than the table.
F-42 RECOMMENDED 3 Declare the footprint polygon and the collision box in the description (section 3.1), so a checker and a human can see what a consumer will do.
F-43 RECOMMENDED 3 Never make an item that must be walked under, through or between (an open pergola, a chair with gaps between its legs); in box mode it is a solid block.
F-44 RECOMMENDED 3 Avoid low obstacles up to extensions.walkability.stepHeightMetres that are not obviously steps (a floor box, a cable cover): a walker steps over them unnoticed.
F-50 REQUIRED 3 Stay within the profile's limits for a whole delivery: limits.maxFileMegabytes, limits.maxVertices, limits.maxTriangles.
F-51 RECOMMENDED 3 Keep each item small: at most budgets.maxItemTriangles triangles (default 2,000), far fewer for ordinary items.
F-52 RECOMMENDED 3 Do not deliver textures with an item.
F-53 RECOMMENDED 3 Use one or two surface colours on an ordinary item and up to four on a feature item; every distinct colour of every item adds a material.
F-60 RECOMMENDED 3 Describe variants in the description file.
F-61 RECOMMENDED 3 Place repeated items as instances: each instance is an element of its own (own GlobalId, own ObjectPlacement), sharing geometry through IfcMappedItem and IfcRepresentationMap.
F-62 REQUIRED 3 Give each instance its own unique GlobalId (guide 1, B-70) and a level to belong to (guide 1, B-13).
F-62a RECOMMENDED 3 Place every instance inside the room it serves, and do not let it extend through a wall or a floor.
F-63 RECOMMENDED 3 Record the item id and version on every instance (ItemId, ItemVersion, F-03) so that a revision of the library can be rolled out by replacing instances.
F-70 REQUIRED 3 Follow guide 1 exactly for light fixtures (section 11) and, when signboards are enabled, for signs (section 12).
F-71 RECOMMENDED 3 Make a fixture's housing and emissive part separate parts so that only the emissive part glows.
F-72 RECOMMENDED 3 Other fixtures (hand rails, handles, hooks, bathroom fittings, planters) are small elements with their own colour, in the classes of section 2.
X-01 REQUIRED 4 Use this layout.
X-02 RECOMMENDED 4 Use lower-case ASCII file names without blanks, forward slashes in every path, and keep paths under 200 characters.
X-10 REQUIRED 4 Put a manifest.json at the top of the package that matches the schema.
X-11 REQUIRED 4 Record the SHA-256 hash (64 lower-case hexadecimal characters) and size in bytes of every file, and include a SHA256SUMS.txt in the plain two-column form (hash, two blanks, path).
X-12 REQUIRED 4 List every file in the package, and only those, in the manifest.
X-13 RECOMMENDED 4 A building delivery has exactly one master IFC file (guide 1, B-03); other files are alternates.
X-14 REQUIRED 4 Keep the whole package within the profile's cap, package.maxPackageMegabytes, when it sets one.
X-20 REQUIRED 4 Give every IFC file, texture set and library item a provenance entry (what it is, where it came from: original, procedural with the script and seed, or a named source; who made it; the licence that applies) when the profile requires provenance (package.requireProvenance, default true).
X-21 REQUIRED 4 State a licence for every asset and a licence.statement for the package when the profile requires it (package.requireLicence, default true).
X-23 REQUIRED 4 When the delivery has terrain, list the patch and its sidecar under terrain/ with their roles, give each a provenance entry, and record the source package name, version and hash and the patch hash in the manifest terrain section, equal to what the sidecar states and to what the check report of the master file found in it, and keep the site request (its building origin, azimuth and floor height must be the file's).
X-22 RECOMMENDED 4 Deliver only content you are free to hand over.
X-30 RECOMMENDED 4 Version the delivery, each texture set and each item with SemVer (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), and give every version a creation time.
X-31 RECOMMENDED 4 Choose the next version number by what changed.
X-32 RECOMMENDED 4 Write notes/changes.md: for each version, the ids added, changed and removed, in plain sentences.
X-50 REQUIRED 4 Never change a delivered version in place.
X-40 REQUIRED 4 Run check_ifc.py on the exact master file you are sending, with the profile, and include its JSON report in the package.
X-41 RECOMMENDED 4 Deliver tables/rooms.csv with the columns roomId, name, occupant, kind (room, circulation, observation, open), enclosed (yes or no), level, levelElevationMetres, floorAreaM2, clearHeightM, buildingId and layer, and list every new Occupant string with the room-id prefix that goes with it and its kind, so a receiving party can add its rules before intake.
X-60 RECOMMENDED 4 When you send a revision, change only what the findings and your own notes name, bump the version (section 4), list what changed in notes/changes.md, and keep every unchanged identifier.
